title: The Constraint / Current Most Limiting Factor
opening: Polishing a lesson cannot help someone who cannot find or open it. Once that problem is fixed, an unclear demonstration might be the next thing preventing learning. The limiting condition depends on the result you want and on the whole route to it.

labels.comparison: Which part of the route is stopping progress?
labels.comparisonIntro: The goal in this example is to learn through a particular lesson. Finding the lesson and understanding its demonstration are different conditions. Compare each case, including the case where both are missing.
labels.rhythmTitle: Check what changes after the intervention
labels.rhythmText: After making the lesson easier to find, inspect what happens when people open it. A different limit may matter next. If you do not know where the result stops, obtaining that observation can be more useful than another improvement. A new opportunity may also be worth more than repairing the existing process.
labels.practice: Find the limit in your own pursuit
labels.practiceIntro: Name the result, trace how it is produced and compare the possible limitations. Keep observations, guesses and missing information distinct before choosing an intervention.
labels.private: This private note is optional. The six required course questions are separate.

labels.sourceQuote:
Current Most Limiting Factor
The Current Most Limiting Factor, or CMLF, is what most restricts the specified
result now. If nobody can find the lesson, polishing a paragraph may have little effect
on its use. If people find it but cannot understand the demonstration, increasing
traffic may amplify the problem. The limit depends on the result and the state of the
whole path.
labels.sampleLoaded: Example loaded. Replace it with your own observations when useful.
labels.accessText: The learner never reaches the lesson. Improving the demonstration leaves that condition unchanged. Inspect where the learner looks, whether the lesson is available there and whether the link opens.
labels.understandingText: The learner reaches the lesson but cannot follow what it explains. Sending more people to the same demonstration does not address that difficulty. Compare the explanation, assumed knowledge and practice task with what the learner can actually do.
labels.coupledText: Making the lesson available leaves the unclear demonstration to address. Improving the demonstration leaves the access problem to address. Both conditions can matter together; you do not have to pretend that only one limitation exists.
